p: John's Gospel opens not with a birth but with a beginning older than the world. Read the five verses first, then take them one at a time.
li: 1  In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
2  The same was in the beginning with God.
3  All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.
4  In him was life; and the life was the light of men.
5  And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.

section.h2: Verse 1 — 'In the beginning was the Word'
p: John reaches back past creation itself. Before there was a beginning to be in, the Word already was.
'Word' translates logos — reason, speech, the expression of a mind. God was never silent.

section.h2: Verses 3–4 — 'All things were made by him'
p: Nothing that exists made itself. Life is not something the Word keeps at a distance; it is in him.
And that life is named as light — the very first thing God called good.
The light is neither overcome nor understood — both meanings sit inside the one word.
To study Scripture is, in part, to learn to see.
